ChauffeurNet advances this approach by utilizing mid-level input representations combined with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to output driving trajectories.
ChauffeurNet enables training on both real and simulated data.

The CARLA simulator serves as a comprehensive open-source platform that facilitates development, training, and validation of autonomous driving models.
CARLA provides flexible sensor and environment configurations.
CARLA provides digital urban assets.
CARLA supports evaluation of various driving approaches including end-to-end learning and reinforcement learning.
CARLA enables evaluation in controlled scenarios with specific metrics.
CARLA offers measurements of agent state and traffic rule compliance.
These measurements are critical for training and assessment.

Early systems such as ALVINN demonstrated the feasibility of end-to-end neural network steering.
ALVINN used relatively small fully-connected networks.
ALVINN used limited data.
Modern CNN-based systems leverage greater computational power and extensive datasets to improve robustness.
